# Demo 3: transaction replay

**Threat.** An attacker (or a faulty network) re-sends payments, status answers, events and reversal notifications, forges or re-uses signed evidence, or answers for the wrong transaction or route, hoping for a second debit, credit or reversal, or a terminal-state regression.

**Trigger.** Track B's replay simulator plus the v1.1 replay cases against the integrated stack on PostgreSQL (seed 101).

Track B replay cases: 23; duplicate reversal postings: 0. v1.1 cases: 13; unexpected outcomes: 0.

| v1.1 case | expected | as expected |
|---|---|---|
| duplicate_payment | same transaction, one DEBIT | True |
| duplicate_event_delivery | nothing newly applied (duplicates; unrepresentable rows dead-lettered again), twin unchanged | True |
| duplicate_status_result | 200 DUPLICATE_EVENT, twin unchanged | True |
| concurrent_duplicate_result | no 204 (already applied), twin unchanged | True |
| wrong_transaction_id | refused UNKNOWN_TRANSACTION | True |
| wrong_route | refused ROUTE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH | True |
| conflicting_authoritative_outcome | refused 409, twin keeps SUCCESS | True |
| old_transaction_version | identical old version: duplicate; altered old version: refused; twin unchanged | True |
| unregistered_event_source | refused UNKNOWN_SOURCE | True |
| invalid_source_signature | evidence stored unverified; no settlement; still unresolved | True |
| expired_evidence | stale signature rejected; no settlement | True |
| answer_for_other_transaction | discarded (WRONG_TRANSACTION); t4 unresolved | True |
| duplicate_reversal_completion | duplicate (200); one REVERSAL posting | True |

Ledger after the attack: integrity True, duplicate check starts 0, second debits 0, second reversals 0, unverified evidence applied 0.

**Enforcement.** Idempotency keys and unique operation ids (one debit), row-locked version CAS (no stale or concurrent second effect), HMAC response verification with key identity and a ±300 s window (forged/expired evidence is stored but never applied), controller intake idempotency and conflict detection (duplicate events change nothing).
